result:
**1. src/pages/Home/common/useController.ts — acquisition never attempted when the access token is already within 25 s of expiry.**
Trigger: the effect registers (mount, token change, visibility→visible, `showTimeout`/`isOnLogout` change) while a parseable refresh-token expiry exists and access expiry is ≤ 25 s away. `scheduleAcquisition` only sets a timer when the delay is positive, and the immediate catch-up call only runs when the refresh expiry is unknown; the catch-up's non-scheduled guard also requires ≥ 25 s, so it cannot fire. A background-throttled timer that is resumed after the 25 s mark lands in the same gap.
Consequence: no refresh request; the dialog appears and the session ends unextended.
Baseline: `setTimeout(..., difftime - 25000)` with a negative delay fired immediately, so a refresh was always attempted.
Uncertainty: the comment says missed deadlines intentionally do not replay, so the resume case may be deliberate; the fresh-registration case still looks unintended.

**2. src/pages/Home/common/useController.ts — repeated refresh calls for an already-expired refresh token.**
Trigger: refresh-token exp is in the past while access is still valid; `reconcileExpiry` runs on the immediate expiry timer, on each visibility→visible transition, and on each effect re-registration.
Consequence: `getRefreshToken()` is invoked repeatedly with no in-flight check; if the service does not dedupe, overlapping (rotating) refreshes can race and drop the session.
Baseline: one timer produced one refresh attempt.
Uncertainty: the pending-refresh mechanism used by the Timeout hook suggests the service may already dedupe.

**3. src/components/Timeout/common/useController.ts — sign-out is no longer awaited.**
Trigger: `continuLogout` after the 1 s wait.
Consequence: the dialog is closed before logout settles, and a rejection from `logout()` becomes an unhandled rejection instead of being handled in sequence.
Baseline: `await logout()` completed before the dialog closed and timers were cleared.
Uncertainty: may be an intentional fire-and-forget change; impact depends on `logout()` and `setOpen` behavior outside the reviewed paths.

Scope: reviewed only the three selected files plus the provided `sessionEpoch` context; service, provider, dispatcher, and view code were not available.
